overall_quality.evidence: Processes and threads are both fundamental concepts in operating systems, but they serve different purposes and have distinct characteristics. Processes are the basic units of execution in an operating system, while threads are the units of execution within a process. Processes are isolated from each other, and each process has its own memory space. Threads, on the other hand, share the same memory space and can communicate with each other more easily. Processes are more resource-intensive and have higher overhead, while threads are more lightweight and efficient.
